I am 74 years old and have been farming these flat lands in Quzhou County since I was a small girl. I never went to school — the characters on paper mean nothing to me — but the soil, the rain, and the seasons have been my teachers for over sixty years. My family has five *mu* of good land near the village well, and my son still lives close by and helps me when the machines need running.

This year, I will do what I have always done: **winter wheat followed by summer maize**. I know these crops. They feed my family, and the grain dealer comes to the village to buy what we do not eat. I do not grow cotton anymore — my back cannot bear the bending and the endless spraying.

In early October, right after National Day, I will sow **wheat** across all five *mu*. I will buy **jimai22** seeds from the village shop — it is a good, steady improved variety that my neighbors also use. Before sowing, I will run the **rotary tiller** to prepare the bed. At sowing, I will spread compound fertilizer and then topdress with urea when the wheat greens up in spring. I will irrigate **three times**: the winter irrigation to protect from frost, the green-up water, and the heading water. That is what my father did, and the well has always given us enough. I will spray twice for weeds and once for insects. If heaven is kind, I expect about **500 kg per *mu***.

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I will plant **summer maize** on the same five *mu*. I will sow **denghai605** — a hybrid seed that costs more but yields well and resists lodging. I will **not till** much; the wheat stubble is already in the ground and there is no time to waste before the rains come. I will put down compound fertilizer at sowing and irrigate **twice**: once when the seedlings are small, and once at the big trumpet stage. I will spray twice for insects and once for weeds. I expect another **500 kg per *mu*** from the corn.

I keep some grain for flour and feeding, sell the rest, and return all the straw to the field. The land has never lied to me, and I do not intend to change what works.
